audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Dentistry bachelor, taught at ACTA in collaboration with Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, combines biomedical and oral-health science with prevention, restorative dentistry and patient care. The compulsory three-year curriculum includes dental-skills training, supervised treatment, evidence-based dentistry and a scientific internship.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial study of human biology, disease mechanisms, infection, immunity, health psychology and prevention, supported by laboratory and research methods. These are meaningful foundations for oral-health interests. The strongest complete UCR programmes, however, develop general biomedical science, patient experience or materials and technical inquiry without sustained study of oral biology, dental disease and restoration. Together these gaps leave dentistry’s defining academic subject matter insufficiently represented.

componentNotes.y1-04: Introduction includes a diagnostic Dutch-language test. A satisfactory test or completion of the required remedial language course is necessary before the module grade is awarded.
componentNotes.y1-09: Preclinical training develops the practical dental skills needed before patient treatment. At least ninety percent practical attendance is normally required.
componentNotes.y2-10: Pass first-year Oral Biology and Cariology, Direct Restorations and Dental Skills 1A, and attend all New Patient practicals within Dental Skills 1B.
componentNotes.y2-04: Pass first-year Oral Biology and Cariology, Direct Restorations and Dental Skills 1A, and attend all New Patient practicals within Dental Skills 1B.
componentNotes.y2-05: Pass first-year Oral Biology and Cariology, Direct Restorations and Dental Skills 1A and 1B, and participate in Dental Skills 2A.
componentNotes.y3-05: The compulsory fourteen-credit scientific internship requires Research Methods and Statistics and Preparation for the Scientific Internship. Scientific work includes literature research and/or contribution to research, culminating in a written report.
componentNotes.y3-07: Pass second-year Prevention, Care Planning, Periodontitis I, Dental Prevention and Dental Skills 2A and 2B. Care of non-complex patients includes oral-health assessment, caries and periodontal treatment, carried out in student pairs with treating and assisting roles.
componentNotes.y3-08: The patient-care curriculum includes intraoral radiographs. Successful preparatory preclinical practicals are required before patient treatment.
componentNotes.y3-09: After six months or more without clinical patient care, students must pass both non-patient and patient competency assessments before resuming clinical practicals. Restorative dental work is a clinical and technical learning line, distinct from the scientific research internship.
componentNotes.y3-11: This compulsory professional-conduct credit is awarded after the other 179 credits. The bachelor prepares for further Dentistry study; it does not itself confer the completed dentist qualification.
